A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original FFHQ and ShapeNet reconstruction, generation, classification, clustering and weight-space experiments, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a multi-category initialization-perturbation visualization in Section 4.4.

M1.justification: The multiplicative LoRA formulation, asymmetric masking, base-model training, hierarchical LoRA encoder and diffusion procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FFHQ at 128×128 and ShapeNet airplane and ten-category settings. The new visualization reuses existing ShapeNet categories and initialization perturbations; it changes the analysis design within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The six representation variants remain the same. Generation retains HyperDiffusion and the same five alternatives, and the encoder ablation retains its with/without comparison. The new visualization uses the existing six variants.

E3.justification: v3 Section 4.4 adds a joint visualization protocol: fit 20 instances from each of five ShapeNet categories at nine perturbation strengths, then embed the converged weights together using t-SNE. Existing reconstruction, generation, classification and ablation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 examines how initialization, category and instance jointly organize weight space, extending the earlier separate perturbation and category analyses. Existing encoder ablation, interpolation and CLIP nearest-neighbor novelty checks are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 still reports averages over 30 instances with standard-deviation shading, and classification/clustering still report statistics from ten randomized runs. The new perturbation visualization adds experimental conditions without changing statistical or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds qualitative findings: MLP variants form nine initialization-dominated modes, whereas multiplicative LoRA variants exhibit category-dominated organization, with additive LoRA intermediate. All five numerical tables match after relocation and renumbering, and earlier qualitative image panels are retained.

T1.justification: The permutation-symmetry proofs, multiplicative decomposition, channel-alignment corollary and metric definitions are unchanged. v2 Section 6 becomes v3 Appendix A with renumbered theorem and corollary labels.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about multiplicative LoRA, structured weight representations and their reconstruction, generative and semantic capabilities. The new Takeaways summarize existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 introduces an organizing-hierarchy interpretation: initialization precedes category and instance for MLP variants, while category precedes instance and initialization for multiplicative LoRA. It interprets this as semantic structure becoming dominant. Existing mechanism discussions and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 Section 8 and v3 Appendix C provide the same architectures, optimization schedules, dataset preparation, diffusion hyperparameters and pipeline. No implementation, resource-reporting or code/data-access change accompanies the new analysis.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 47 cited works and the same positioning relative to weight-space learning, HyperDiffusion, functa and neural-field research. Bibliographic presentation changes do not alter citation membership or positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds Takeaways, moves reconstruction from Section 4.1 to Appendix E, separates visualization into Section 4.4 and relabels the appendices. Most existing prose is retained. Appendix G's table references were not consistently updated after renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redesigns the presentation with a shaded title/abstract/Takeaways panel, new typography and heading styles, changed spacing and widespread figure/table reflow. It adds Figure 6, relocates the reconstruction table and moves Algorithm 1 later in the appendix; existing visual evidence is preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 Section 4.4 and Figure 6 make the joint influence of initialization and category directly inspectable, modestly strengthening v2's separate stability and semantic-structure analyses. The gain is qualitative and limited, with methods and numerical results unchanged. Stale table references in Appendix G introduce a small editorial cost but do not outweigh this additional evidence.
